value.body: Beyond classroom teaching, education organisations and ed-tech firms hire people to design curricula, write and review learning content, train teachers, and support learners. Employers include ed-tech companies, school chains, publishers, assessment firms and education NGOs or government programmes.

items.label: Common roles
items.value: Curriculum designer, content developer / subject expert, instructional designer, teacher trainer, academic counsellor

items.label: Employers
items.value: Ed-tech firms, school groups, publishers, education NGOs

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A degree in the subject plus a teaching qualification (B.Ed or ITEP) is common for pedagogy and content roles. Hiring is direct — through applications, sample tasks and interviews; classroom experience is often valued.

value.title: At a glance
items: Ed-tech hiring has been volatile, with widely reported layoffs after 2022; NGOs and school groups can be steadier.
Some ed-tech 'counsellor' roles are mainly sales with targets — read the job description carefully.
Content and curriculum skills transfer to publishing and instructional design in corporate training.
